items.t: ABB Keeps Buying Back Stock While Beijing Blocks Its Robotics Sale
sum: ABB repurchased 575,000 of its own shares between 29 October and Wednesday, the Swiss engineering group said Thursday, continuing a buyback programme it announced on 6 February. Cumulative purchases since the programme began on 9 February now total 12,593,273 shares.

The buyback runs alongside a far less settled matter: the sale of ABB's robotics business to SoftBank, which China's outbound investment security review body has blocked. SoftBank informed ABB of the decision, and ABB said the two companies remain in close dialogue and are working constructively on the transaction. The agreed deal carries an enterprise value of USD 5.375bn.

Swiss broadcaster SRF floated two possible routes forward — a restructuring of the transaction, or a separate buyer for the China units. Neither has been resolved, and the outcome of the sale remains open. Media reports have questioned whether the agreed disposal can close at all; Reuters reported a decline in ABB shares on Thursday tied to the Chinese veto, with market commentary pointing to uncertainty over the deal and ABB's China business.

Analysts have kept their footing even as the deal wobbles. UBS reaffirmed its "Neutral" rating on Wednesday with a price target of CHF 88, as reported by dpa-AFX — a confirmation rather than an upgrade or downgrade. Analyst Andre Kukhnin based the call on findings from a conversation with ABB chief executive Morten Wierod, whose tone the study described as confident. Goldman Sachs, by contrast, cut its target on 30 October to CHF 79 from CHF 82 while holding its "Neutral" rating. Same stance, different numbers.

Away from the transaction, ABB on Monday reported two orders from Southwest Aluminum (Group) Co., Ltd. covering integrated automation, process control and digital solutions for two cold rolling mills in Chongqing. Both plants are scheduled to be fully operational by the end of 2027.

In a separate regulatory disclosure, a member of ABB's management acquired 170 ABB registered shares on 31 October under the Employee Share Acquisition Plan, a transaction valued at CHF 10,098 according to the SIX register filing.
The stock rose 0.8% on Friday. ABB's next confirmed event is its Group Capital Markets Day on 18 November 2026 in New Berlin, USA.

ABB's Robotics Exit Hits a Chinese Wall as Buyback Rolls On
sum: ABB has run into a regulatory roadblock that could reshape a deal worth billions. The Swiss engineering group confirmed that China's foreign investment security review authority has blocked SoftBank's acquisition of ABB's robotics operations inside China, a decision first reported by Reuters. The prohibition targets the Chinese portion of the business, yet it casts a shadow over the wider transaction rather than amounting to a confirmed cancellation of the entire sale.

The economics behind the disposal were straightforward. ABB Robotics turned over USD 2.3 billion in 2024, roughly 7% of group revenue, while posting an operating margin of 12.1% — well short of the 18.1% managed at group level. Shedding a unit that trails the parent's profitability made strategic sense, provided the separation could be executed on workable terms.

The financial stakes were laid out when the transaction was agreed in October 2025. ABB anticipated net cash proceeds of about USD 5.3 billion after transaction costs, plus a non-operational pre-tax book gain of roughly USD 2.4 billion. The agreed enterprise value stood at USD 5.375 billion, with completion originally targeted for mid-to-late 2026.

Those projections remain contingent on closing. Both companies say they are continuing to work constructively toward the deal, which keeps a negotiated outcome alive as long as talks produce an implementable agreement. What hangs in the balance now is the structure, the proceeds and the timetable of any completed sale — and only once those are fixed can investors gauge how much of the expected benefit ABB actually retains.

China is the largest market for ABB Robotics, so the veto lands squarely on a core part of the business. According to the Financial Times, Chinese authorities worry that robotics data could flow abroad and be used to train AI models. Any revised structure that keeps the Chinese operations inside the takeover would have to address those security concerns.
Investors marked the stock down 4.3% on the news, reflecting concern that the sale is now harder to pull off. The pullback captures that uncertainty rather than any confirmed collapse of the deal.

ABB stock draws mixed analyst view despite fair-value discount
sum: Simply Wall St updated its ABB Ltd analysis on Wednesday, November 4, presenting a constructive but cautious view of the industrial group. The review puts the company at the intersection of electrification, motion and automation, while highlighting the valuation and execution questions that investors face after a strong period for the shares.

The report cites a market capitalization of CHF 127.6 billion and coverage from 29 analysts. Its consensus assessment places ABB at a 13.9 percent discount to the platform's estimated fair value, with a consensus target of CHF 82.86. Those figures relate to the Swiss listing and are separate from the euro quotation in Germany.

Simply Wall St identifies data-center and grid demand as important elements of the longer-term growth case. ABB supplies electrification and automation products to utilities, industrial customers, transport operators and infrastructure projects across Europe, the Americas, Asia, the Middle East and Africa.

The analyst material is not uniformly bullish. One narrative points to operational strength and market caution, while other assessments frame data-center and grid demand as potential drivers of margins and earnings. A more defensive view highlights margin pressure and integration risks. For investors, the combination means that order momentum must translate into reliable delivery, profitable growth and disciplined capital allocation.

The same report forecasts earnings growth of 9.09 percent per year and records earnings growth of 23.9 percent over the past year. It also lists a one-year share performance of 20.10 percent for the Swiss listing. These figures describe the analysis page's reference market and should not be treated as a euro-market performance comparison.
ABB stock traded at 78.09 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:45:49 CET on Wednesday, November 4, 2026.

ABB Q3 FY 2026 Earnings Show Record Orders Outpacing Revenue on Data Centers
sum: ABB’s third quarter showed demand for its electrification portfolio running well ahead of what it can deliver in the near term, with data centers again leading the way. New direct current technology and a joint venture in Japan point to where management wants the next leg of growth to come from.

The News: ABB (NYSE: ABB) reported third-quarter results for the period ended September 30, 2026. Revenue was $9.70 billion, up 14% year on year (YoY) on both a reported and comparable basis, versus consensus of $9.77 billion. By business area, Electrification revenue was $5.42 billion (up 21% YoY), Motion revenue was $2.32 billion (up 11% YoY), and Automation revenue was $2.13 billion (up 6% YoY). Orders reached a record $12.06 billion, up 40% YoY, for a book-to-bill ratio of 1.24 and an order backlog of $32.26 billion. Operational EBITA rose 24% YoY to $2.03 billion, with the margin expanding 160 basis points to 20.8%. Net income attributable to ABB was $1.18 billion, down 2% YoY, and basic earnings per share (EPS) was $0.65, down 2% YoY.

“ABB delivered record order intake and improved operational performance with strong cash flow and return on capital. We advanced our leading position in direct current technology, and today we progressed on M&A with a new electrification joint venture with Mitsubishi Electric,” said Morten Wierod, CEO of ABB.

Analyst Take: The first thing we notice here is a strong demand story: Comparable orders rose 40%, well ahead of revenue, pushing the backlog to roughly the size of ABB’s entire FY 2025 revenue base. The Operational EBITA margin was the best Q3 result in ABB’s history, yet basic EPS slipped on a non-cash hedge linked to the Rotork acquisition and a tax charge tied to separating ABB Robotics, now a discontinued operation.

Investors fixed on that dip and a slight revenue shortfall, and the shares fell as much as 6.7% on the day. I think that reaction misreads a quarter whose bigger news was the Infinitus DC launch and the Mitsubishi Electric joint venture, but also misses the point of where ABB looks to be headed.
Electrification orders also climbed 70% on a comparable basis to $7.67 billion, the seventh straight quarter of sequential growth. Note that this lifts the business area’s backlog to $16 billion.

ABB stock: Record orders reinforce higher 2026 outlook
sum: ABB reported record third-quarter orders on October 20, with data-center demand driving growth across its electrification and industrial technology businesses. ABB stock traded at 77.00 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 14:35 CET on Friday, October 30, 2026, 1.23 percent below the 77.96 euros recorded in our October 30 report at 10:38 CET.

The company said in its Q3 2026 results that orders rose 40 percent year over year to USD 12.055 billion. Revenue increased 14 percent to USD 9.701 billion, while the 1.24 book-to-bill ratio showed that order intake exceeded quarterly revenue.

ABB said data-center orders grew at a triple-digit rate during the quarter. Two of its three business areas contributed strongly to the increase, and demand was positive across most customer segments.

Operational EBITA rose 24 percent to USD 2.026 billion, lifting the margin by 1.6 percentage points to 20.8 percent. Net income attributable to ABB declined 2 percent to USD 1.181 billion, as higher net finance expenses affected earnings per share.

ABB expects fourth-quarter comparable revenue growth to remain broadly similar to the third quarter. The Operational EBITA margin is expected to soften sequentially, although less than the usual seasonal pattern. The outlook excludes a positive contribution of about CHF 240 million from completed property sales.

For full-year 2026, management expects a positive book-to-bill ratio, comparable revenue growth in the low-teens range and reported Operational EBITA margin improvement of at least 270 basis points year over year. The key investor question is whether strong orders convert into sustained revenue and margin progress.
For the real-time quote of ABB stock, investors should watch order conversion and execution in the coming quarters.

sum: ABB Ltd (CH0012221716) reported a third-quarter book-to-bill ratio of 1.24, while demand in its data center segment rose at a triple-digit rate. The detail changes the reading of the company's recent automation push because electrification demand, rather than robotics alone, is carrying the strongest order momentum.

In its October 20, 2026 results release, ABB said third-quarter orders reached USD 12,055 million, up 40 percent from USD 8,606 million a year earlier. The same release said revenue increased 14 percent to USD 9,701 million and Operational EBITA rose 24 percent to USD 2,026 million.

ABB's CEO summary says the data center segment delivered the most notable growth across customer groups. That gives the order figure a more specific explanation than a broad industrial recovery: power distribution and energy-efficiency projects are becoming a larger part of the demand mix.

The operating conversion also improved. Operational EBITA margin reached 20.8 percent in the third quarter, compared with 19.2 percent a year earlier, while operating cash flow rose 5 percent to USD 1,862 million. ABB expects full-year comparable revenue growth in the low teens and an Operational EBITA margin improvement of at least 270 basis points.

sum: ABB (ISIN CH0012221716) announced on October 20, 2026, that it will take a controlling 51 percent stake in a new joint venture with Mitsubishi Electric's low-voltage power distribution business, according to ABB. ABB stock was trading at EUR 75.81 at Lang & Schwarz on October 22, 2026, at 9:18 a.m. CEST, 1.60 percent below the Xetra close of October 21, 2026, at EUR 77.04.

The transaction gives ABB control of the Japanese business and expands its position in one of the world's largest electrification markets. The contributed Mitsubishi Electric operations generated JPY 102.0 billion in fiscal year 2025 revenue, while ABB will pay JPY 79.0 billion for the controlling stake and related sales operations outside Japan, according to ABB.

ABB expects the venture to reach at least a 20.00 percent Operational EBITA margin within five years. The company also said the combined businesses have an enterprise value of USD 890.0 million and an enterprise-value-to-EBITDA multiple of 11.10 based on fiscal year 2025 figures.

The deal arrived with a strong Q3 operating update. ABB reported orders of USD 12.06 billion for the third quarter of 2026, up 40.00 percent from USD 8.61 billion in the third quarter of 2025, while revenue increased 14.00 percent to USD 9.70 billion from USD 8.49 billion, according to ABB.

Operational EBITA rose 24.00 percent to USD 2.03 billion in the third quarter, and the margin reached 20.80 percent versus 19.20 percent a year earlier. Net income attributable to ABB fell 2.00 percent to USD 1.18 billion, showing that stronger operating performance did not lift every earnings measure.

ABB expects fourth-quarter 2026 comparable revenue growth to remain broadly similar to the third quarter, while the Operational EBITA margin should soften sequentially. The next full-year results are scheduled for January 28, 2027, according to MFN.
Analyst expectations add a valuation counterweight. UBS retained a Neutral rating and a CHF 88.00 price target in its October 13, 2026 assessment, as reported by Finanznachrichten.

Global Chip Stocks Plunge as US Inflation Spike Revives Fed Rate-Hike Bets
sum: Semiconductor shares across Europe, Asia and the United States tumbled on Thursday, extending a global rout in technology stocks after hotter-than-expected US inflation data rekindled bets that the Federal Reserve may need to raise interest rates further.

The selloff, which began on Wall Street and swept through Asian markets before hitting Europe, was broad-based and severe. German chipmakers Infineon and Aixtron each fell about 8% to 9% in early European trading, while Dutch equipment maker ASM International dropped by a similar margin. ASML, the region's most valuable technology company, slid 5.5% to 5.6%, and BE Semiconductor lost 5.7% to 6.5%. France's STMicroelectronics slumped 6.5% to 7.5%.

Smaller European names were hit even harder. Suss MicroTec fell as much as 9.4%, while Elmos Semiconductor and Swiss chip and lighting company ams OSRAM declined between 3.6% and 7%. Siltronic, Soitec and Technoprobe tumbled between 6.5% and 10%, and AI-exposed industrial stocks including Nokia, Legrand, Schneider Electric and ABB slid 4% to 5%.

In the US, memory chipmakers bore the brunt of the selling. SK Hynix slumped 6.7% and Micron fell 4.1% in premarket trading, while Western Digital and Seagate Technology each lost more than 4%. Nvidia, the bellwether for AI-related chip demand, slid 1.8%, and Intel and AMD dropped more than 3% each.

The catalyst for the rout came Wednesday, when the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that US consumer prices rose 0.6% in September from August, lifting the annual inflation rate to 3.7% from 3.4% a month earlier. The monthly figure matched economists' expectations, but the annual reading came in a tenth of a percentage point above the 3.6% consensus forecast.

Core inflation, which strips out volatile food and energy costs, rose 0.3% on the month and 2.6% from a year earlier, up from 2.4% in August. Both readings exceeded forecasts by a tenth of a point. Surging energy costs were once again the primary driver of the increase.

The data immediately reshaped expectations for the Fed's policy path. Traders briefly priced in roughly even odds of a rate increase at the central bank's meeting later this month before pulling those bets back.

Grab These ETFs to Capitalize on the Physical AI Wave
sum: Artificial intelligence (AI) is evolving at an extraordinary pace, moving beyond chatbots and content generation into something far more consequential: machines that can perceive, reason, and act autonomously in the physical world. Currently, physical AI represents the convergence of AI with robotics, autonomous vehicles, drones and smart manufacturing systems.

The growth prospects for this market reflect this momentum, with the global physical AI market projected to grow from $1.50 billion in 2026 to $15.24 billion by 2032, representing a 47.2% CAGR (as predicted by Markets & Markets).

For investors, this transformation is putting companies working on physical AI in the spotlight, and by extension, exchange-traded funds (ETFs) holding these stocks are emerging as compelling low-risk investment options to capture the trend.

Before examining these funds, it is important to understand the industry's key players and the extent to which physical AI is transforming the market. This broader perspective can help investors assess the growth opportunities and make informed investment decisions.

Physical AI marks a fundamental shift from AI as a digital tool to AI as a system capable of driving real-world outcomes. As NVIDIA’s CEO mentioned last year: “AI’s next stage is called physical AI, where AI interacts with the physical world, and it means robotics.”

Several companies are currently leading this charge, with NVIDIA NVDA at the center of the physical AI ecosystem. The company provides full-stack AI computing for physical AI and robotics through its GPUs, Jetson edge platforms, and Isaac robotics framework. NVDA has partnered with companies like Unitree to release open humanoid robot reference designs to accelerate academic and industry research.
Beyond humanoids, NVIDIA's Jetson and Hyperion platforms power autonomous tractors, mowers, delivery bots (like Serve Robotics), and L4 autonomous mobility solutions.

Schneider Electric Strikes Historic $22.6 Billion Deal to Acquire PTC
sum: French industrial group Schneider Electric announced a definitive agreement to fully acquire U.S. industrial software company PTC Inc. in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $22.6 billion, marking the largest deal in the group's history. The move comes as major global industrial companies race to strengthen their capabilities in artificial intelligence and digital infrastructure tied to data centers.

Under the terms of the offer, Schneider will pay $205 per share, representing a 42.3% premium over PTC's last closing price, according to deal data. The total enterprise value is estimated at approximately $23.7 billion including debt. The closing is expected to be completed by the third quarter of 2027, pending regulatory approvals and shareholder consent.

PTC is headquartered in Boston and provides specialized software solutions for product design, manufacturing, and maintenance across multiple sectors, including automotive, aerospace, and medical technology. The U.S. company has also benefited from growing demand for its AI-powered tools, making it a strategic target for Schneider, which seeks to fill remaining gaps in its software portfolio.

Following the announcement, PTC shares surged sharply in pre-market U.S. trading, while Schneider's stock fell as much as 10% on the Paris stock exchange, marking its largest single-day decline since January 2025. The divergence reflects investor concerns about the scale of financing required for the deal and its impact on leverage levels.

Lucas Ferhani, an analyst at Jefferies, said the acquisition "fills one of the last remaining gaps in Schneider's software portfolio." He added that the deal significantly strengthens the French group's software capabilities in a sector experiencing intensifying competition.

Olivier Blum, CEO of Schneider Electric, described the deal as one that would create "the most integrated software and AI platform in the industrial sector." Neil Barua, CEO of PTC, affirmed that by joining Schneider, the company would gain "greater resources and capabilities to accelerate innovation and expand its geographic presence."

ABB Bank Completes Acquisition of a Controlling Stake in Davr Bank
sum: Baku, September 14, 2026 - ABB Financial Group has successfully completed the acquisition of a controlling stake in Davr Bank, a commercial bank operating in Uzbekistan. The transaction was registered on 10 September 2026 at the Tashkent Stock Exchange.

Under the terms of the agreement, ABB Bank acquired 51 million ordinary shares of Davr Bank, representing a 51% ownership stake in the bank. The total value of the transaction amounted to 1.646 trillion soums (approximately USD 140 million).

Following the completion of the transaction, Davr Bank will commence operations in the Uzbekistan market under the "ABB Davr" brand as a universal bank, providing a wide range of banking services to individuals, small and medium-sized enterprises, as well as corporate clients.

Currently, Davr Bank serves more than 2 million customers, employs over 1,800 people, and operates 43 branches and service centers across the capital and regions. The bank's total assets exceed USD 2 billion equivalent. Davr Bank maintains a strong position, particularly in financing small and medium-sized enterprises.

The official opening ceremony of the "ABB Davr Bank" project was held on 23 August 2026 during the state visit of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev to Uzbekistan, with the participation of the Presidents of Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan.
ABB Financial Group's strategic vision for the Uzbekistan market is outlined in an interview with ABB Bank's Chairman of the Management Board Abbas Ibrahimov.
Following ABB Bank's acquisition of a controlling stake in Davr Bank, the bank's international ratings have also started to improve.

items.t: ABB India Q2 Results FY27: Date, Expectations, Watch
sum: ABB India Q2 Results FY27 Preview: Results Date, Expectations and the Numbers That Will Decide the September 2026 Quarter
ABB India share price Rs 7,387.00 on 8 September 2026, down 0.63%. Q2 FY27 results date not confirmed. Q1 FY27 net profit Rs 362.30 crore. Q2 FY26 base a profit of Rs 409.04 crore.

The ABB India Q2 results FY27 announcement is the next scheduled earnings event for ABB India Ltd., the Indian arm of the ABB group, supplying electrification, motion, process automation and robotics equipment to industry, utilities and infrastructure. The stock traded at Rs 7,387.00 on the NSE on 8 September 2026, down 0.63% from the previous close of Rs 7,434.00, about 6.8% below its 52-week high of Rs 7,924.50 and 59.3% above its 52-week low of Rs 4,637.50.

What makes the ABB India Q2 results print worth watching is the base it faces. The September 2025 quarter delivered Rs 3,394.67 crore of revenue and a profit of Rs 409.04 crore, while the most recent quarter on record, Q1 FY27, produced Rs 3,651.54 crore and a profit of Rs 362.30 crore. Everything below is built from those reported figures rather than from any forecast.

The ABB India Q2 results date for FY27 is not confirmed. As of 8 September 2026, ABB India Ltd. had not filed a board meeting intimation with the NSE or BSE for the September 2026 quarter, so any date circulating before that filing appears should be treated as unverified.

What can be stated is the regulatory boundary. Listed companies in India must publish quarterly results within 45 days of the end of the quarter, which places the outer deadline for the September 2026 quarter at 14 November 2026. Companies also have to give the exchanges prior intimation of the board meeting that approves the results, so the ABB India Q2 results date becomes public through that filing rather than through any advance announcement.

The ABB India Q2 results FY27 print covers 1 July 2026 to 30 September 2026. Small and mid-cap companies more often report in the second half of that window than in the first, so late October or early November is the range to watch for ABB India.

ABB India Shares Surge 10% To Record High as India Order Growth Sparks Rally
sum: Mumbai, July 16: ABB India share price surged as much as 10% on Thursday to hit a 52-week high after its Swiss parent reported a robust set of second-quarter results and highlighted strong order momentum from India, reinforcing optimism about the subsidiary’s growth prospects. The rally came despite ABB India yet to announce its own June-quarter earnings, with investors betting that the healthy demand environment would translate into strong domestic performance.
The sharp rally made ABB India one of the top gainers in the capital goods space. As of writing the stock was up 7% at Rs 7,707.

The immediate trigger for the rally was ABB Ltd’s second-quarter earnings announcement, which exceeded market expectations on the back of resilient demand across its electrification and automation businesses.
The stock is racing after positive commentary by parent on India ops. Source: NSE
More importantly for domestic investors, the global engineering major flagged robust order growth from the India region, highlighting the country as one of its strongest-performing markets.

ABB Ltd reported that orders from the India region jumped 81% year-on-year in the June quarter. The India order figures disclosed by the Swiss engineering major include business generated by both its listed subsidiary, ABB India, and its unlisted operations in the country.

The commentary reinforced expectations that ABB India’s upcoming quarterly results could benefit from healthy order inflows, particularly amid continued investments in power infrastructure, industrial automation and data centres.

ABB to acquire Advantics, expanding Direct Current portfolio
sum: - Strengthens ABB’s industry-leading technologies for Direct Current applications
- Advantics’ technology offers up to 99% efficiency for demanding power conversion applications
- Acquisition targets energy expansion and data center growth

ABB is acquiring Advantics, a specialist provider of Silicon Carbide-based power conversion solutions based in France. The acquisition expands ABB's Direct Current (DC) portfolio and positions the company to serve accelerating demand for efficient DC solutions across data centers, industrial microgrids, power generation and EV infrastructure. Financial terms were not disclosed. The transaction is expected to close by Q4 2026.

The IEA expects electricity’s share of final energy consumption to rise from 20 percent today to around 36 percent by 2035. By using advanced semiconductor technology to control more of this electrical power, ABB’s DC solutions minimize repeated AC/DC conversion and maximize efficiency.

The acquisition of Advantics adds a high-efficiency Silicon Carbide power conversion technology to ABB’s broader DC portfolio, strengthening the building blocks needed to design, protect, convert, distribute and manage power in new electrical architectures with higher power density, resilience and efficiency. Combined with ABB’s expertise in protection, distribution, digital control and system-level engineering, the acquisition supports the development of DC systems that maximize efficiency, energy storage and flexible power sources.

Massimiliano Cifalitti, President of ABB's Smart Power division, said: "We invest continuously in technology and talent to support global energy expansion. ABB offers industry-leading Direct Current solutions, and Advantics' power converter technology and world-class engineering talent are a perfect match, adding compact, high-efficiency capabilities that will strengthen our offering for data centers, industrial microgrids, and EV infrastructure. Together, we will accelerate the development and delivery of next-generation DC solutions."

items.t: BSE Capital Goods Index Falls Over 1.5 Percent on 7 July 2026 as Cochin Shipyard Slips More Than 4 Percent
sum: BSE Capital Goods index down over 1.5% on 7 July 2026. Cochin Shipyard -4.21%, GE Vernova T&D -3.11%, CG Power -2.3%, Siemens -2.29% lead the fall among 20-plus capital goods stocks.

The BSE Capital Goods index declined over 1.5 percent on 7 July 2026, making it one of the weakest sector indices in an otherwise firm broader market. Cochin Shipyard led the fall, slipping more than 4 percent, followed by GE Vernova T&D, CG Power and Siemens, all down over 2 percent.

The broad-based decline across engineering, power equipment and defence manufacturing names came even as the Nifty 50 and Sensex traded modestly higher, underlining stock-specific and sector-specific pressure rather than a market-wide risk-off move.

The single largest drag on the BSE Capital Goods index is Cochin Shipyard, which fell over 4 percent as the government's Rs 1,400 floor price offer for sale opened on 7 July, pulling the market price toward the discounted OFS level. When a heavyweight constituent falls sharply on supply-side news, it drags the entire index lower even if other names are only mildly weak.

Beyond Cochin Shipyard, the breadth of the decline, with virtually every major capital goods name from GE Vernova T&D to Kaynes Technology trading lower, points to broader profit booking in a sector that has rallied hard over the past year on India's capex and defence indigenisation themes. After such sharp multi-quarter gains, capital goods valuations leave little room for disappointment, making the sector vulnerable to even modest negative triggers.

Beyond Cochin Shipyard, GE Vernova T&D India fell over 3 percent, and CG Power, Siemens and ABB India each declined more than 2 percent. Mid-sized names including KEI Industries, Data Patterns, BHEL and Siemens Energy also traded with cuts of around 2 percent, showing the sell-off was not confined to any single sub-segment, spanning power transmission, defence electronics, industrial automation and heavy electrical equipment alike.
Investors tracking the BSE Capital Goods index should watch whether the sell-off is a one-day event tied to the Cochin Shipyard OFS or the start of a deeper correction after the sector's strong run.

items.t: GE Vernova, CG Power shares a buy: 'Overreaction' as 4 Chinese firms enter power tenders, says Nomura
sum: The 7-8 per cent selloff in shares of grid equipment makers GE Vernova T&D India Ltd, CG Power and Industrial Solutions Ltd, Hitachi Energy India Ltd and Siemens Energy India Ltd was an 'overreaction' to the Ministry of Finance's decision to allow four China-origin manufacturers to bid for power tenders in India, Nomura said on Monday.

Noting that the order explicitly states it creates no precedent, Nomura said market players read it as a competitive threat and sold off listed power-equipment stocks such as GE Vernova T&D India, CG Power, Hitachi Energy India and Siemens Energy India. For now, Nomura has retained its 'Buy' rating on CG Power (target price: Rs 1,100) and GE Vernova T&D India (Rs 5,675). It does not cover Siemens Energy India and Hitachi Energy India.
